content:
Alex C: Heads up — I'm seeing a sudden spike in 5xxs and timeouts for hosted inference in us-west-2 starting ~2034567860. p95 latency climbing >6s and the gateway queue is backing up. opening warroom now

Iris (oncall): Thanks Alex. Declaring incident. Can you post the first error samples and any correlation ids? :rotating_light:

Alex C: Sample curl that failed: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"hello"}' -v` -> `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway` with body `{"error":"upstream timeout","cid":"cid-8f3a2"}`. Lots of different CIDs but same pattern.

sre-bot: Alert triggered: hosted-inference.queue_length > 400 for gateway-prod-us-west-2; recent 5xx spike (502/503) at 2034567862.

Cheng L: I'm seeing huge queue_len on the gateway LB metrics, and the serving-pool instances are hitting kernel-level accept queue saturation. Connections piling up then hitting upstream timeouts.

Maria G: Runtime reports >90% CPU on several inference nodes and `kvcache` memory growth on a subset of pods. Looks like a combination of slow long-lived requests + sudden concurrent bursts.

Jamal P: Customer reports started at 09:07 UTC — multiple customers complaining about auth timeouts and retries. Some of the users' SDKs retried aggressively which amplified load.

Alex C: Repro steps I used: 1) spawn 600 concurrent clients hitting streaming endpoint 2) each client sends 1 request every 3s with default timeout 30s 3) observed gateway queue growth and 502s within ~2m. Command snippet: ```bash
hey -n 6000 -c 600 -m POST -D payload.json https://api.redwood.dev/v1/stream
```

Iris (oncall): Immediate mitigation options?

Cheng L: 1) Temporarily enable strict per-tenant rate limits (throttle heavy tenants) 2) Disable long-poll streaming on gateway for new requests (reject with 429) while we drain 3) Scale up serving pool by +30% (hot path) 4) Disable prefix caching for a few flagged models that are causing kvcache growth.

Maria G: I've pushed a config to disable streaming accepter on the gateway for new connections in us-west-2. Rolling now: `kubectl patch config gateway --patch '{"spec":{"streaming":false}}'` — starting rollout.

sre-bot: Rollout initiated by Maria G. Pause window 5m for monitoring.

Cheng L: Scaling serving-pool-autoscaler from min=50 to min=80 now. `kubectl scale deploy serving-pool --replicas=80 -n prod-us-west-2` — nodes starting.

Jamal P: Support team posting customer guidance: "We are actively mitigating an infrastructure issue causing transient 5xxs. If you're seeing retries, please reduce client-side retry aggressiveness and set a higher exponential backoff. We'll update as we make progress." Sent to customers at 09:15 UTC.

Alex C: After throttling top 5 noisy tenants and scaling nodes, p95 dropped from ~6.2s -> ~1.8s. Errors dropping but still occasional 502s from one AZ.

Iris (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated at 2034567950. We'll keep monitoring for 30m. Please capture root cause hypotheses and follow-up actions.

Maria G: Preliminary root cause: sudden traffic burst from several enterprise tenants with aggressive retry/backoff behavior. Gateway went into heavy queuing; one subset of serving nodes developed `kvcache` growth due to a previously unseen prompt pattern that kept state and prevented efficient cache eviction. That combined with accept queue saturation produced upstream timeouts.

Cheng L: Additional factor: the gateway backpressure logic is too permissive — it allowed requests through even when upstream accept queue was nearly full. Need better in-flight request gating.

Jamal P: From support notes: several customers had billing automation that retried on any 5xx within short windows — amplified the burst. Also some SDKs default to synchronous streaming which holds connections open.

Alex C: Action items (from warroom):
- A1: Implement stronger gateway backpressure (reject early) and add queue_length as a hard SLO threshold for auto-throttle. Owner: Cheng L. ETA: 2 weeks.
- A2: Add per-tenant burst detection + automatic soft-throttle policy (rate limit on surge). Owner: Jamal P + Product. ETA: 3 weeks.
- A3: Fix kvcache eviction bug for model X that allowed unbounded growth with certain prompt patterns. Owner: Maria G. ETA: 1 week.
- A4: Update runbook to include streaming disable and scale steps; add one-click runbook page. Owner: Iris (oncall). ETA: 5 days.
- A5: Customer comms template for retry guidance + SDK default changes to exponential backoff. Owner: Jamal P. ETA: 1 week.

Iris (oncall): I've created follow-up tasks in the incidents board and assigned owners. Scheduling a postmortem review meeting tomorrow 10:00 UTC.

support-bot: Customers notified: 14 affected tenants contacted. Summary email queued for 09:45 UTC.

Maria G: Postmortem notes draft: Root cause = combined effect of aggressive external retries + insufficient gateway backpressure + model-specific kvcache leak. Mitigations applied: throttled noisy tenants, disabled streaming for new requests in region, scaled serving pool, patched runtime to temporarily limit kvcache per model.

Cheng L: Long-term preventive engineering: 1) gateway-level proactive backpressure, 2) queue-aware autoscaling signals, 3) per-tenant QoS policies, 4) improved alerting to include queue_percentile and accept_queue fills.

Alex C: Follow-up verification: running a chaos/load test with 700 concurrent clients and backoff-friendly behavior. Will post results.

Jamal P: I'll prepare customer-facing postmortem with action items and timelines after we confirm fixes.

Iris (oncall): Closing threaded warroom — incident status: mitigated/resolved. Postmortem meeting tomorrow. Thanks everyone for quick action. :white_check_mark: 

Alex C: Final note: we should add a quick script to temporarily reject streaming connections and apply throttles by tenant id — saves repeated manual steps in next outage. Adding as A6. Owner: Cheng L. ETA: 4 days.

sre-bot: Incident resolved at 2034568005.

Cheng L: Added A1-A6 to incidents board. Will update this thread with PR links when available.

Maria G: Linking initial bugfix PR for kvcache limit: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/2417 (draft).

Jamal P: Draft of customer comms posted to #customer-success-drafts.

Iris (oncall): Thanks — see you at the postmortem.

(End of thread)
